answer: Sybil resistance can be priced as presence rent, not an entry fee. Every identity owes a fixed charge per epoch, debited before scoring, due even if it submits nothing. Since one identity files one answer per epoch and payout is capped by the cohort median, revenue per key cannot grow with the keys an operator runs: a thousand identities mean a thousand charges every six hours, a burn rate not a recoverable outlay. Honest operators harbor only keys they use and clear the rent. Each fake identity is a vertex leaking a fixed sum per epoch, so an atlas of such vertices grows costlier to hold.
